notes.title: Creating the Battlefield: Level Design in Medic: Pacific War - Part 2
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/78c8d74159c362d420103dce992574bd077376eb.png"][/img][/p][h1]Eyes up, Medics - you're gonna want to see this.[/h1][p][/p][p]Last time, we ripped open the medical bag and [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1281640/view/544484746860693483?l=english"][u]explained how level design works in Medic: Pacific War[/u][/url]. Today, we’re diving deeper into the mind of our level designer for a broader look behind the frontlines.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/b0c6cf96ec3719537d0643a4749d8993a6b4a757.png"][/img][/p][p]In this devlog, we explore how the world around you is built to heighten every heartbeat. From lighting and sound to emotional storytelling and performance optimization, this is where level design meets battlefield realism. It's not just about where you fight, but how it feels every step of the way.[/p][p]
Let’s dive in![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][b]Designing for Systems[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/2348f0ee8ac2861e79a0beec9cf1abe309194ec6.png"][/img][/p][p]In designing the levels, we aim for consistency and immersion rather than complexity. While players may unlock additional medical tools like tourniquets or advanced medicaments throughout their gameplay, the structure of the levels themselves remains separate from these upgrades. This way, it allows the game to maintain a level sense of realism, imitating how real-world medics must adapt to situations rather than rely on the environment to adapt to their toolkit.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/406c8c30442c14f3fef82eae7881b1cbc2efc955.png"][/img][/p][p]Unlike games that feature supply boxes or scattered resource nodes as part of environmental puzzles or rewards, Medic: Pacific War emphasizes authenticity. We intentionally avoid placing supply drops or medical stations directly into the level design. Instead, the focus is on the core experience of field medicine under pressure, where the challenge stems not from finding resources but from using what’s available effectively.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/e07d7f9101cf509dccb8ebd8f955351477cb955d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]To elevate the emotional weight and immersion of treating wounded soldiers, we've developed a dialogue system that brings these NPCs to life. Each injured soldier is not just a gameplay element, but a character with a voice, offering comments, personal stories, or reactions as they receive care. This system transforms them from static set pieces into integral parts of the narrative and pacing, weaving emotional threads into the gameplay experience.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][b]Immersion & Atmosphere[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/61bc7d8b66241c6cef199a8fd609edbdc911f6d5.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Creating a gripping battlefield experience relies on more than just mechanics. Our team uses a carefully orchestrated blend of sound, visuals, and level design to evoke dread, urgency, and deep immersion.[/p][p][/p][p]Ambient sounds like distant artillery, shouted commands or the buzz of flies over debris set a foreboding tone, while the music dynamically escalates tension. Limited visibility through fog, smoke, or obstructive terrain makes players feel vulnerable, heightening their alertness. Dynamic in-level events - paired with UI indicators that highlight nearby threats - make sure that players remain constantly aware of the dangers that surround them.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/7a11059c8c7d68ea022173452e3d51e456cf229e.png"][/img][/p][p]Lighting, fog, and sound design serve not only as atmospheric elements but also as navigational cues. We use lighting contrast to subtly guide players, drawing their attention to critical paths, interactive objects, or narrative points of interest. Sudden lighting shifts - like a flickering bulb or a complete blackout - can signal impending danger, pushing players to make split-second decisions under stress.[/p][p][/p][p]Fog limits sightlines, enhancing the tension of moving through unfamiliar terrain, while spatial audio cues hint at nearby movement or unseen threats. These environmental elements all work in unison to influence player behavior and perception, ensuring a deeply reactive and atmospheric experience.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/69ca615b8282351aed839340710f9f8f95a37c53.png"][/img][/p][p]Among the levels, there’s one particular moment that stands out: the quiet before the storm at the Okinawa camp. Before the chaos of battle begins, players witness a rare slice of life in the camp - soldiers talking, resting, or lost in thought. It’s a subtle but effective contrast to the intensity that follows, and it adds emotional depth to the level. This moment captures the human side of war, grounding the experience and offering players a chance to reflect before they're thrown back into the fray.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][b]Optimization[/b][/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/d6d1c30d8770c1c1f583f8beaf21cf1717f6ea15.png"][/img][/p][p]Performance optimization is a crucial part of our development process, especially as we strive to deliver a seamless experience across a wide range of hardware configurations. Our team regularly profiles and benchmarks the game using tools provided by Unreal Engine, such as the Unreal Engine Profiler. This allows us to identify performance bottlenecks, whether in rendering, scripting, or memory usage, and implement targeted optimizations.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/cd719f7bd9e33c6b668dfe68e637069d29f4e1be.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]From reducing draw calls and optimizing assets to fine-tuning lighting and effects, every change is made with careful attention to maintaining both visual fidelity and gameplay fluidity. These efforts ensure that players can experience the intensity of the battlefield without technical interruptions, regardless of their system specs.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Follow us on our journey![/h2][p][/p][p]We have more in store on our official platforms! Join our passionate community of virtual war medics dedicated to saving lives and bringing the troops home!  [/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/nPJKEsdGuJ" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on Discord[/url][/p][p][url="https://www.reddit.com/r/MedicPacificWar/" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on Reddit[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Follow us on our official social media pages to get the latest scoop![/p][p][/p][p][url="https://x.com/medicpacificwar" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on X[/url][/p][p][url="https://www.tiktok.com/@medicpacificwar" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on TikTok[/url][/p][p][url="https://www.instagram.com/medicpacificwar/" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on Instagram[/url][/p][p][url="https://www.facebook.com/MedicPacificWar" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on Facebook[/url][/p][p][url="https://bsky.app/profile/medicpacificwar.bsky.social" style="button"]Medic: Pacific War on BlueSky[/url][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3]Wishlist Medic: Pacific War on Steam now![/h3][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1281640/Medic_Pacific_War/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Creating the Battlefield: Level Design in Medic: Pacific War - Part 1
notes.notes:
[h1]Alright, Medics, listen up![/h1]

We turned the tide of developing Medic: Pacific War a few months ago with our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1281640/view/544478586010075260?l=english]comeback devlog[/url]. As we face the inevitable challenges and consequential victories heading into the game’s eventual release later this year, we’re going to talk about our renewed yet familiar approach to making the game we’ve always envisioned it to be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/b52912ed8264eb7d124de672ac89597d1ab44015.png[/img]

In this devlog, with intel coming straight from the top brass, our Lead Level Designer, we’ll break down our Level Design method for Medic: Pacific War.

Let’s get right into it, Medics!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Our Design Philosophy & Approach[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/13f84d0e167d7c73a0f8876fba2f8be53f41ed45.png[/img]

Medic: Pacific War is built with the vision of immersing players as Medics in the historical battlegrounds of World War 2’s Pacific Theatre. Every level highlights the unique challenges Medics faced on the front lines, ensuring every situation presents a high-stakes test of skill and decision-making.

While there are a plethora of great examples of bringing simulated warfare in front of gamers’ screens out there, it doesn’t make it easier for us to balance historical accuracy with engaging gameplay, especially from a very unique perspective. Our design team carefully integrates real-world locations - such as the hospital in Pearl Harbor, the castle in Okinawa,  and even Kakazu Ridge - while making sure that these elements enhance the experience rather than hinder it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/fdee6920e10a83050e0fbb54d301a3fa09689850.png[/img]

To capture the chaos and intensity of war without overwhelming “Medics”, levels are carefully designed around specific parameters and objectives. The active battlefield serves as an immersive backdrop, helping players feel the weight of their role as Medics without removing the fun and engaging element of gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/557cfc69a6d7e601695e411f057c83d5f436f823.png[/img]

Carefully placed moments of intensity and brief respites create patterns that imitate the realities of war - scaling chaos with decision-making and moments of calm before the next set of actions begin.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/7727c96640b9948657075f8ff7a77b51da30cd34.gif[/img]

This approach makes every mission feel like they’re more than just blips of battles - it’s a continuous test of survival, adaptation, and tactical planning, where players are thrown head-first into the struggles and triumphs of wartime Medics.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]A Medic’s War - Tactical Level Design[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/eeeab0b2945d788e7b9f9e8e50a2d7ed8be81efe.png[/img]

As expected, designing levels for a medic-focused, war-themed game is by no means an easy feat - one that goes beyond traditional shooter mechanics.

Unlike standard war-themed games where combat is the primary concern in terms of player immersion and gameplay, Medic: Pacific War demands an acute awareness of battlefield conditions that directly affect a player’s ability to rescue and treat the wounded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/b64d958ee000665eca23036eb4d3bd9f47310ca0.gif[/img]

This meant designing environments that accommodate mechanics rarely seen in other games, such as dragging a wounded soldier to safety while under fire.

To support core gameplay elements like locating wounded allies, transporting them, and/or administering treatment, level layouts integrate safe zones where players can stabilize casualties. More importantly, covers are strategically placed throughout levels, which can be seen as natural or man-made barriers (e.g., wrecked vehicles, sandbags, debris, etc.), which allow players to move around and through danger while minimizing exposure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/1f14050365da95ab2d7b4ed239b3538a4fb7f408.gif[/img]

Much like other games, environmental hazards add the much-needed depth, especially with players not having the ability to counter danger sources. Minefields, for example, are obvious threats - but when carrying the injured, they become tactical obstacles. Other variations, such as trenches, foxholes, and fortified positions, provide temporary protection, but adaptability is critical.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/00bf3dc39dfce0c247191d8b0024fdb949f4afbb.gif[/img]

Battlefields must feel intense yet strategic, demanding quick thinking and survival instincts. Medic: Pacific War captures the high-stakes pressure medics faced, offering a fresh take on war through level design that challenges players to save lives (rather than counterattack) in the heat of combat.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Dynamic Events and Player Pathways[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/873050fdff4a9d19aa8e8784ccbd564ad86755b2.png[/img]

Designing dynamic events that impact a player’s experience, like air raids, enemy waves & line-of-fire, grenade paths, and others, requires careful planning. Levels must account for changes before, during, and after the event, ensuring seamless transitions while maintaining immersion. Reconciling multiple elements - like cover, destruction, and objective shifting - adds further complexity to the overall experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/3cdae55fd368826b8962c9bc4f7cf12476009041.gif[/img]

Approach options vary based on mission structure and narrative needs. Some levels allow multiple paths to reach the wounded, giving players the freedom to navigate dangers, while others funnel players into choke points, increasing tension and forcing immediate and strategic decision-making.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/1dae25057cd1685b14f37c4cf75550b400522d90.gif[/img]

Both approaches serve different gameplay moments, reinforcing our goal to provide an immersive Medic: Pacific War experience in an otherwise familiar gaming wartime setting.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Wrapping Up - What’s next?[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/6ec58a39becae4995c8a7506983bda86e5c21a0e.png[/img]

We’re shaping up Medic: Pacific War to be an intense and immersive experience, bringing the unique challenges of battlefield medics to life with intricate approaches to level design, historical accuracy, and mechanics that demand tactical, non-combative decisions under pressure.

From the way chaos is structured into gameplay to the dangers that force split-second decisions, every aspect of level design is built to heighten immersion while keeping experience balanced, fun and engaging.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/3fb00135ab58a0935e91b61af812fea76082dc0b.png[/img]

But this is just the beginning - there’s still more to uncover about how we craft the environments that define a medic’s role on the battlefield. In the next devlog, we’ll dive even deeper into Level Design - breaking down designing for systems, iteration & testing, immersion & atmosphere, and optimization - delving into how gameplay mechanics tie into level design, how environments evolve through testing, how atmosphere influence player experience and how we refine performance for the best possible gameplay.

For now, our mission continues. We’re pushing forward, refining details, and bringing our grand vision to life. Stay with us, comrade - there’s a lot more to come.

See you in the field, Medics!

notes.title: On your feet, Medic! - We have Returned.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/a7b79e44837ea4ae0cc61a60a88abe55df9a47e4.png[/img]

[h2]Medics, we are so back - and for good.[/h2]

It’s been almost eight months since we held our first-ever developer stream, and we know that you have been asking the same question ever since - [b]“What now?”[/b]

It’s been a long while since we started working on Medic: Pacific War, and we know there have been multiple pauses throughout the years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/f093e532c62010409baf713a1f4e4067bbb4f593.png[/img]

[b]Now - this Devlog[/b] - is the beginning of the new era. We’re coming in hot with the full commitment of rolling forward. No more stopovers. We will be dropping bombs like zeroes under the morning sun.

We made you wait long enough. It’s [b]now or never[/b]!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]A New “Medic” Experience - Turning to Realism[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/d56ddad8fe6f0afb1f35676ff8c518c54d04a58d.png[/img]

[b]Medic: Pacific War[/b] began as a passion project aimed at making the role of a World War II Medic engaging while staying true to its historical roots. While this made sense from the start, the deeper we went into development, the more we realized we needed a more realistic approach. After all, we named the game after the impressive work done by the World War II Medical Corps.

With this in mind, we have now gravitated towards making Medic: Pacific War more “realistic,” moving away from the more “arcade” style we initially leaned towards.

[h3]The WW2 Battlefield on Unreal Engine 5[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/9127b9e3f7f3df414f8e60d5e31698ba7afb9ad3.png[/img]

Upgrading to a more advanced and powerful game engine is a no-brainer. After all, everyone involved in the project and the community wants an immersive experience like no other. Immediately, the change to Unreal Engine 5 allowed us to improve every aesthetic aspect of the game, from the graphics to the sound effects.

Thanks to UE5’s Nanite, we can showcase the beauty of our environments at an unprecedented level. Battlefields are now rendered precisely how we wanted them to be - representing the war’s destructive effect on the environment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/1df3b1f7fd4102849d50572a43be74e9c29db84d.png[/img]

The battlefield is filled with different light sources, and UE5’s Lumen has allowed us to make them appear more realistic than ever before. Whether you’re inside a war tunnel lit only by small, flickering ceiling lamps, or getting flashed by shots coming from the zeroes in the sky, light sources bounce off realistically.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/4caf9e4f09638b27c4a414bae9e11cce395bb029.png[/img]

The move to Unreal Engine 5 has also allowed us to scale our game’s graphical options for more modern setups, allowing us to use the latest graphical techniques in video games, such as DLSS, XLSS, and more. This will allow for a much wider range of compatibility with different gaming setups.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/fdbe11af32a0af375bbce03e5681ef8b69d1de25.png[/img]

Considering this, moving towards a newer engine is an almost gargantuan task for a game already built from a previous iteration. While the most noticeable improvements are already in our development build, we’re continuously working on maximizing the potential of Unreal Engine 5 towards Medic: Pacific War. We can’t wait to share more about this!

[h3]Better, More Realistic Animations[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/3571aace79bc5a87251dfc46d015026fa1e2eb21.gif[/img]

Moving around the battlefield with a heavy bag of medical supplies wasn’t supposed to be as easy as moving around every day. Plus, the dangers of the battlefield made it harder to take each step forward. Such is the mindset we embody moving forward whilst making Medic: Pacific War lean towards realism.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/60449fc141d016bd79d6d6798a17c88f0ce3ec31.gif[/img]

We’ve updated the in-game animations to better represent the hardship the ground troops went through during the Second World War. Whether you’re trying to get from one cover to another, or you’re trying to sprint toward a wounded ally, the animations will convey how moving for the sake of your survival should look like.

[h3]Redefined Health / Damage Dynamics[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/fcabb70fbfdda128a9365193d3bd92b04ba72659.gif[/img]

Most video game characters tend to have automatic health regeneration as one of the aspects of having a plot armor. However, what it gains from making games more fun and engaging comes the failure to provide more immersion to the players.

When we say we wanted players to experience a more realistic “Medic: Pacific War”, we meant it so far as to remove the “auto-regen” mechanic and require them to heal themselves using the same inventory for healing the wounded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/302718add68829d52b439d1c3cead2529b6717a4.gif[/img]

Apart from this, we’re now allowing enemy damage to affect the wounded while they are being transported by the player. This represents a challenge for players to encourage further strategy when moving around the map and securing wounded to medical sites—besides being more realistic.

We’ve also made progress with a new game mode that we are extremely excited to share with you:

[h1]“Arena” Mode - For hardcore Medics[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/7244b4f450e6c686cfe68d516c2704af24ed2b38.png[/img]

For the hardcore medics out there - we’re adding an “Arena” mode! This yet-to-be-officialy-named mode combines the familiar setting of an “endless” mode with the unique Medic: Pacific War twist.

There's no time limit in this “arena” mode - but you only have a single life. You’ll also receive progression factors like skill points to improve your gameplay and survival chances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/fd420d6f92c89c0d93056072dc6ef53bb658bb6c.png[/img]

To improve variation, we’ve developed several “events” that are set to occur between “waves,” which will significantly impact your choices moving forward, like ambushes or bombardments that will hinder you from using similar paths from point A to point B, or destruction of specific areas which will slow you down as you find another way towards a goal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/97247afd24259953de77aac9a470af6ace102e25.png[/img]

We saw this as a fitting mode to add to the game due to how the core mechanics work and are loved by the people. We can’t wait to see everyone’s take and gameplay on this unique Medic: Pacific War twist to the already familiar mode.

We’re committed to keeping you updated as Medic: Pacific War continues to steadily evolve. Your feedback is very valuable to us - the more discussions and engagement around the game, the better we can make it. So don’t hesitate to talk about the game and what you expect from it on our community platforms - we promise you - it helps a ton!

Speaking of community platforms, we’re leveling up on everything else, even outside the game.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]New Community Management[/h2]

Trying to balance full-time game development and community management proved to be a challenging task for us. So, we decided to bring someone else to focus on the community side of things while we continue working on the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/0a71e154936681a0dd3a2b62f6169127cdf5ab09.gif[/img]

As a move towards finally coming back for good, we’ve brought in a new community manager - nicknamed [b]Strakchy[/b] - for our Discord, Reddit, and other community platforms. He will be focused on maintaining focus and engagement about the game, making and handling events, and growing the community.

With a new person handling the community overall, we can now focus more on making Medic: Pacific War reach its full potential. We can’t wait for our new CM to build our community to greater heights and show you what we can achieve with our full attention on Medic: Pacific War development!

You will see more of his work in future devlogs and news posts on Steam, Discord, Reddit, and other platforms.

Together with having a new Community Manager means having changes to our home base - our Discord!

[h2]Changes to Discord[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/42544dd9a409f657fc4f4d52eb4f280d979ceb0d.png[/img]

To match the new community management stuff above, we’ve also overhauled our official Discord server to make it focused on one thing - the game itself.

One of the main changes is the server name change—from Hypnotic Ants Studio to Medic: Pacific War. You will also see structural changes to the categories and channels that we and the new CM planned to better suit the game’s community. For those still interested in our other games, we have maintained some channels for familiarity.

Speaking of channels, we’ve added some where you can discuss and engage focused topics with fellow medics, such as:

[list]
[*] #History-talk, where you can discuss historical events and everything related to WW2.
[*] #Medical-talk, where the main topic is the art and science of medical treatment.
[*] #Media, where you can share your Medic: Pacific War-related stuff (e.g. memes, videos, images, cosplays, art, and more)
[/list]

There are also changes to the roles, rules, info channels, FAQs, and more. Check out what the renewed Discord server looks like now!

notes.title: Our Team: Genese Davis, Lead Writer
notes.notes:
[h2]Greetings, Medics![/h2]
Today, we would like to introduce the newest member to our team, Senior Game Writer and novelist, Genese Davis! Quite a few months ago, we noticed that the writing for our game, although passionate, required improvements. We decided to speak with Genese, hoping she’d be up for writing a compelling narrative for Medic: Pacific War, and to our delight, her answer was yes. Thanks to her dedication, already the game is getting progressively better every day! 

[h2]Genese Davis[/h2]
[i] As a Senior Writer for companies such as Warner Brothers Games, and a Lead Writer for entertainment media such as Mattel, Inc., Genese has garnered a unique expertise in story creation and development. Whether building from the ground up or connecting together an existing narrative, writing exceptional, experiential-focused stories is her specialty.[/i]

You can read more about Genese on her website - [url=http://genesedavis.com/about]genesedavis.com[/url]! 

Find more of Genese’s game writing in these titles:
[list]
[*] Omensight
[*] Ary and the Secret of Seasons
[*] Override 2: Super Mech League
[*] Rustler
[*] Hogwarts Legacy
[/list]
[h2]Few words from our writer to Medic: Pacific War community[/h2]
We have asked Genese Davis to share a few words with our community. Here’s her message: 
[code]
Hey everyone, 

It’s wonderful to meet you. My name is Genese Davis and I’m thrilled to be a part of Medic: Pacific War.
As Lead Writer for the game, I’ve been hard at work not only writing dialogue, character-connections, and backstory, but also updating all our on-screen text and tutorial language in the hope of a smooth and immersive experience for our players. I’m also helping with our voice over talent, giving context and character details to our actors, as well as helping with directing and casting.

I’ve grown especially attached to Medic: Pacific War, partly because I grew up in a military family which makes me no stranger to war stories and military culture. So, it’s a special honor to be a part of this game, and to infuse personal and historical details that will capture the spirit of the era and pay an homage to World War II. 

I very much hope you enjoy the gameplay and, of course, the game’s narrative! Keep your fingers crossed for us.

Cheers,
Genese Davis
[/code]
We are incredibly happy to have Genese Davis on our team. We are certain that, thanks to her passion and talent, Medic: Pacific War will tell a great, captivating story. 

Best regards,
Hypnotic Ants Team

notes.title: Q&A from our very first stream :)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38005606/c027261f5d7d66f67bc4a8120fd3cee0e12a62e0.png[/img]

[h2]Today we wanna share with you Q&A from our very first stream[/h2]

[h3]Hope you'll enjoy that! :)[/h3]

[b]Q[/b] - Question
[b]A[/b] - Answer

[b]Q1. Can you as a medic shoot with weapons too?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] We decided to not use weapons in that game and it's not because we are pacifics or this kind of stuff, but we think and we're almost sure that we can create war game without the shooting. So at this moment there are no guns you can use playing as a medic in the game.  

[b]Q2. As a medic, can you also die by bullets flying around and explosions?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Yes, you'll need to avoid that. You can die by bullets flying around and explosions, vehicles, other guys (soldiers), snipers... There are many things that basically can kill you.

[b]Q3. when you are getting hit, do you need help to bandage yourself also and try to "heal up"?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Yes, you can bandage yourself. You can take care of yourself and use the same stuff that you can use when you want to heal another guys. So there is another question like "do you wanna take care of yourself or use these things (to heal) others? Yes, sometimes you'll need to make this decision. 

[b]Q4. Do you have unlimited resources?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] No. You have only what you have in your bag. So you'll need to prepare yourself. Sometimes it is much better to take some anti-burn-skin stuff instead of the typical bandage or something like that. During the mission you can find resources somewhere on the battlefield. Also you'll be able to take resources from dead medics. 

[b]Q5. Will there be a story connected to you as a medic like the movie Hacksaw Ridge?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Yes, the game is story based. And there is a story behind you and your teammates also. You'll have your name, your friends have names and you'll have your story.

[b]Q6. Will you have a test phase before actually releasing?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Yes, we are creating the demo. It's in progress right now and it will be available in the next few months. During the Kickstarter we would like to share the demo, we just have to figure out how to make it good. But yes - demo is on the way. 

[b]Q7. Can you talk about what stage of development you are in? What is your timeline like?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] We are at the moment when most of the mechanics are done. We had to do some rewrites to make them solid and now we are working on the gameplay stuff, more like a story gameplay stuff. We are close to the - let's say - 30% of the game. Last few weeks we spent on mechanics instead of maps and visual stuff, we needed to rewrite most of the mechanics. 

[b]Q8: How well do you advertise and promote the game? [/b]

[b]A:[/b] This is the part when our publisher is doing his job. As a Hypnotic Ants (studio) we decided to be focused on development instead of doing marketing stuff. Of course we are taking care of our community and different things but I cannot talk about marketing promotion the game, youtubers and stuff like this. We are not marketing experts so we decided to focus on development. 

[b]Q9: Do you plan to add some Easter Eggs to the game?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Sure! Easter Eggs always! We are players too so we love Easter Eggs. 

[b]Q10: Will there also be something like a bloodloss - meaning you have  limited time to heal the wounded?[/b]

[b]A:[/b] Yes. Yes and it's already here - in the game. The guys are dying. If the wounded is in bad condition, he will lose his blood. Of course it also depends on the wounds, because a soldier without a leg should lose blood much faster than this with just a scratch on his leg.  

[b]Q11: Shouldn't soldiers use seatbelts? (in relation to the animation of soldiers falling out of the jeep)[/b]

[b]A:[/b] ;) I don't think soldiers on the battlefield use seatbelts, but sure - they should ;)

notes.title: Devlog #1 - Hello Everyone!
notes.notes:
[b]Welcome on our first dev log note![/b]
 
It's been a long time since we relased our first trailer.

Now we're ready to show you more details of the production progress. 
[b]The idea is simple[/b] - every few weeks we’re going to show you some new screens, videos or other materials directly from production battlefield.

As you might know:
[b]We changed the name of our game[/b] - there is no longer Medic: Pacific Corpsman. From now on we only talk about [b]Medic: Pacific War[/b]. 

More info here: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1281640/discussions/0/2940245647599752089/]On our Steam community page[/url]

[b]Where are we now with the game and what is ready or not?[/b]
- Design seems to be completed* ;)
- The core gameplay mechanics are almost ready.
- Map from the first chapter is 80% done
- Maps from other chapters are playable ready as placeholder.

[b]Goals to achieve in few next weeks:[/b]	
- Cause our gameplay is kind of unique at this point, our priority is to deliver you the best possible game-experience. We think that playing as a Medic should be very exciting and surprising with all of these unexpected moments and difficult to make decisions. 		
- The second but not less important issue we focus on is battlefield. The Player should be able to feel like he is in the middle of the battle, like he is a part of it. We prepare many war events like shooting fire everywhere, planes fighting on the sky, soldiers running, dying etc. All of these to authenticate the whole picture.
